market_context: United States; FDA sodium nutrient-content claims
title: Low Sodium, Reduced Sodium, or No Salt Added: They Are Not Equivalent

seo.title: Low Sodium vs Reduced Sodium vs No Salt Added
seo.meta_description: In the U.S., low sodium means 140 mg or less per serving/reference amount, reduced sodium means at least 25% less than the reference food, and no salt added means salt was not added during processing.
seo.search_intent: Explain the difference among low-sodium, reduced-sodium, and no-salt-added claims in the United States.

excerpt: “Low sodium” limits the amount present, “reduced sodium” compares a product with its regular version, and “no salt added” describes processing. A no-salt-added food can still contain sodium naturally or from other ingredients.
content_html:
A can marked “no salt added” can still show sodium on the Nutrition Facts label. That is not a contradiction: the three common front-of-package phrases describe different things.

Low sodium uses an absolute limit

FDA defines “low sodium” as 140 mg of sodium or less per reference amount, with related serving-size rules. “Very low sodium” and “sodium-free” use still lower limits.

Reduced sodium is relative to a reference food

A “reduced sodium” product generally has at least 25% less sodium than an appropriate reference food. If the original food is very salty, the reduced version can still contain hundreds of milligrams per serving.

No salt added tells you what was not added

“No salt added” or “unsalted” means salt was not added during processing. Sodium may still come from ingredients naturally containing sodium or from other sodium-containing components, so the product is not automatically sodium-free.

Compare milligrams, not just the claim

For a real choice, compare the same serving size and the sodium line on Nutrition Facts. Low is an amount, reduced is a comparison, and no salt added is a formulation statement.

faq.question: How much sodium is allowed in a low-sodium food?
faq.answer: FDA generally sets low sodium at 140 mg or less per reference amount.

faq.question: What does reduced sodium mean?
faq.answer: Generally at least 25% less sodium than an appropriate reference food.

faq.question: Can no-salt-added food contain sodium?
faq.answer: Yes. Sodium can be naturally present or come from ingredients other than added table salt.
